papers.title_en: An Equivariant Filter for Spacecraft Nonlinear Relative Navigation with Range and Bearing Measurements
papers.authors: Gil Serrano, Bruno J. Guerreiro, Pedro Lourenço, Rita Cunha
papers.evidence: 航天器近距操作与自主交会的相对导航
papers.tldr: 空间接近操作与自主交会中，相对导航至关重要。非线性相对轨道动力学具有等变性，并具备半直积李群对称结构。本文利用该对称性设计等变滤波器 EqF，将滤波动力学提升到李群上，估计追踪航天器与目标的相对位置和速度，并保持问题几何一致性。仿真验证了滤波器性能与有效性，为空间相对导航提供了一种几何一致的非线性滤波方案。
papers.abstract_en: Relative navigation is a fundamental task in space proximity operations and autonomous rendezvous. The nonlinear relative orbital dynamics are equivariant and admit a semidirect product Lie group symmetry. This property is used to design an Equivariant Filter (EqF). The filter estimates the relative position and velocity between a chaser spacecraft and a target by lifting the filter dynamics to the group, while respecting the underlying geometry of the problem. Simulations demonstrate the filter's performance and effectiveness.

papers.title_en: DreamSat-Bench: Development and Initial Testing of a Testbed for AI-Based Pose Estimation from 3D Reconstruction
papers.authors: Alex Posadas-Nava, August Berne, Giovanni Lavezzi, Kareena Shah, Alejandro Carrasco, Josiane Uwumukiza, Giacomo Battaglia, Paolo Panicucci, Minduli C. Wijayatunga, Victor Rodriguez-Fernandez, Richard Linares
papers.evidence: 面向交会与近距离操作的AI相对导航测试平台
papers.tldr: 针对无先验几何模型的非合作航天器相对导航难题，本文提出模块化交会接近操作测试床 DreamSat-Bench。它统一 MuJoCo、Isaac Lab、LeRobot，用机械臂复现三维轨迹，实现软件与硬件在环贯通。平台将生成式单视图三维重建 DreamSat 与 FoundationPose 零样本 6-DoF 跟踪组合评估，量化重建时延、网格分辨率、轨道距离与光照几何对位姿精度的影响，并给出硬件在环初步验证。
papers.abstract_en: This paper presents the development and initial testing of DreamSat-Bench, a modular rendezvous and proximity operation testbed designed to benchmark AI-based relative navigation techniques. By integrating a software- and hardware-in-the-loop robotic pipeline, the platform enables a seamless transition from digital simulation to physical reality. DreamSat-Bench unifies state-of-the-art robotic learning tools such as MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot into a single benchmarking platform, utilizing robotic arms to trace 3D trajectories. The platform allows for extensive customization of orbital environments and lighting to evaluate the simulation-to-reality gap. We demonstrate the testbed's utility by evaluating an end-to-end vision-based navigation pipeline that pairs DreamSat, a generative AI framework for single-view 3D reconstruction, with FoundationPose for zero-shot 6-DoF tracking of unseen spacecraft. Initial testing explores mission-representative orbital segments, including fixed-point station-keeping and fly-around characterization. Through a series of parametric studies, we quantify the impacts of reconstruction latency, mesh resolution, orbital range, and illumination geometry on pose estimation accuracy. Finally, a preliminary hardware-in-the-loop campaign qualitatively validates the physical deployment of the pipeline, identifying target symmetry and accumulated tracking drift as critical factors for robust navigation. DreamSat-Bench provides a rigorous framework for maturing autonomous navigation with unprepared space assets in the absence of prior geometric models.
